title: Free and cheap fun
description: Good days do not have to cost much — ideas for fun that leave your budget intact.

body.heading: Rethink what fun costs
paragraphs: Many of the best memories — a picnic, a long walk with a friend, a library find, a home movie night — cost little or nothing. Spending and enjoyment are linked far less tightly than adverts suggest.
Try listing ten free things you genuinely enjoy. Keep the list on your phone for the moments when 'there is nothing to do' really means 'I usually pay for entertainment.'

body.heading: Libraries and community gems
paragraphs: Libraries lend far more than books: films, games, tools, and sometimes passes to local attractions. Parks, community centres, and school or university events often run free activities worth discovering.
Swapping is fun too: a clothes swap, a book swap, or a skills swap with friends gives everyone something new without anyone spending.

body.heading: Plan one paid treat
paragraphs: Cheap fun works better when it is not a punishment. Budget one paid treat you truly look forward to, and enjoy the free days around it without feeling deprived.

takeaway: Keep a list of free fun you love, and save paid treats for the ones that matter most.
